summary: User requests ability to use PostgreSQL read-only replicas to offload SELECT queries from primary database for performance improvement, but maintainers explain this violates Temporal's strong consistency requirements needed for correctness.
userImpact: Users operating large Temporal deployments cannot leverage database read replicas to reduce load on the primary database server.
rootCause: Temporal's persistence logic requires strong consistency guarantees (read-after-write) for almost all operations; read replicas provide only eventual consistency, risking unexpected errors or execution getting stuck.
proposedFix: Implement custom DataStore layer via WithCustomDataStoreFactory server option to add replica support, or consider exposing lower SQL plugin injection point (noted as future consideration by maintainers).
workaround: Users can inject custom persistence implementation using WithCustomDataStoreFactory server option to implement replica routing themselves.
keyQuote: Temporal logic assumes database is strongly consistent for almost all the write operations. Violating read after write consistency can easily cause a request to return an unexpected non-retryable errors
